analyst.summary: Pidilite's FY26 volume acceleration is real - underlying volume growth stepped up to 11.1% for the full year and 15.3% in Q4FY26 alone, aided by the GST 2.0 paints rate cut (28%->18%, Sep-2025) and an active construction cycle - and margins expanded 280-310bps as VAM costs eased from their 2022 peak. But that margin tailwind is reversing right now: on 10-May-2026, three days after the Q4 print, the MD flagged a fresh 40-50% weighted-average raw-material-basket inflation from the West Asia conflict, with Fevicol prices already up 12-15% since April and more hikes under consideration - a live risk to the very volume/margin combination that drove the recent re-rating attempt. FY26 PAT growth (+17.9%) is also flattered by an easy year-ago base (a Rs 72cr Brazil-subsidiary divestment loss embedded in FY25), and new-growth optionality has narrowed (lost the AkzoNobel/Dulux bid to JSW; Haisha paints still pilot-stage; the Pargro lending foray dormant). At ~66x trailing P/E - below Pidilite's own 5-year/10-year average multiples but still a rich premium to specialty-chemicals peers - my reverse-DCF reads the market pricing growth close to my own ~11% forward estimate on a generous single-stage basis, tighter on a realistic two-stage build. Hold: quality is intact, but this is a rich multiple being tested by a live cost shock, not a comfortable position to add to.
